title: The SEC Wrote "Possible Ponzi Scheme" in 1997. It Ran Until 2009

lines.say: Nineteen ninety-seven. S.E.C. examiners in Fort Worth review a Houston firm selling CDs from Allen Stanford's offshore bank.
lines.show: 1997. SEC examiners in Fort Worth review a Houston firm selling CDs from Allen Stanford's offshore bank.

lines.say: Their conclusion, as quoted by the agency's own inspector general: Possible misrepresentations. Possible Ponzi scheme.
Examiners came back in nineteen ninety-eight, two thousand two and two thousand four.
An enforcement inquiry opened in nineteen ninety-eight was closed after three months. The report found no meaningful effort to stop the fraud until late two thousand five.
lines.show: An enforcement inquiry opened in 1998 was closed after three months. The report found no meaningful effort to stop the fraud until late 2005.

lines.say: The bank kept selling until February two thousand nine, when a federal judge put it in the hands of a receiver.
lines.show: The bank kept selling until February 2009, when a federal judge put it in the hands of a receiver.

lines.say: Stanford was convicted, and sentenced to one hundred ten years.
lines.show: Stanford was convicted, and sentenced to 110 years.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
